data.cultural_impact: The name Sumran holds great significance in the Islamic culture as it symbolizes the love for agriculture and appreciation for nature, which is deeply embedded in the Islamic way of life. The name is a reminder of the importance of growing food, caring for livestock, and maintaining gardens and farms, as mentioned in several Hadiths and Quranic verses.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Sumran represents the idea of being a caretaker of God's creation, as Muslims are encouraged to be good stewards of the earth and all its resources. It is also believed that through farming, gardening, and other agricultural pursuits, individuals can find peace, contentment, and closeness to God. Ultimately, the name Sumran reflects the idea that our physical world is interconnected and that we have a role to play in nurturing and caring for it.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun describes Sumran as a Berber ruler in the Maghreb, who conquered several cities in al-Andalus and North Africa during the late 14th century.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun's history of the Berbers (Al-'Ibar)

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi mentions Sumran as a military commander under the Egyptian Sultan Qaitbey in the late 15th century, who led an unsuccessful campaign against the Ottomans near Cyprus.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi's history of Egypt (Kitab al-Mawā'iz wa-l-I'tibār fī Khitāt Dhūl-Nūn al-Masrī)
